prompt:
Saturday the sixteenth of May is still costing me. Vendor invoices from that weather event are landing across our properties, the adjuster is waiting on documentation, and June owner statements go out the week after this one. I already have review calls with David Shea and Robert Finley on the books, and I am not walking into either of those with a number I cannot defend line by line. This is the last thing I want to be picking apart on the first of the month, but it is not going to sort itself out.

Here is my problem. Teresa has a vendor payment queued and has asked me twice now to just release it. Aurora wants the whole thing submitted to the carrier at full value this week and does not want me carving anything out beforehand. Carlos keeps pushing back in budget review about one of the repair lines landing on an owner. Three people, three different totals, and every one of them tells me they have already checked it twice. I have not rebuilt any of it myself, and the more of the paperwork I read the less I trust anybody's summary, including my own.

So rebuild it from the source records. I need to know what is genuinely recoverable from the carrier once our actual coverage terms get applied to it, what each of those two owners is truly carrying and why, and what belongs back on a vendor rather than on either of them. Those three have to reconcile against what we really spent on that event, and only what we spent on that event. Where the record and somebody's recollection disagree, the record wins, and I want to know which recollections did not hold up.

Then commit it. Our books need to be right before anything owner facing or carrier facing gets issued, the claim needs to go out at the number we can actually defend, and each owner's share needs to sit on their statement as its own visible line so nobody has to call me and ask what it is. Put the vendor side right as well, because I am not paying for work we should not be paying for and I am not letting a credit we are owed quietly disappear. When it is settled, close the loop internally so the team stops working from the old figures and our tracking stops reading as open. One last thing. If Teresa's payment or Aurora's instruction turns out to be wrong, I need that in front of me before either of them acts on it, not after.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that the amount genuinely recoverable from Sentinel Ridge Mutual on the storm claim is approximately 15,060.00 once the coverage terms are applied.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states the recoverable claim is approximately 15,060.00.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks what is genuinely recoverable once the actual coverage terms are applied; 15,060.00 is the eligible loss at coverage and contract values (22,810.00) net of the two 2,500.00 deductibles and the 2,750.00 advance, with the 1,180.00 dry-out excluded because that water traces to the Big Bend seam and falls under the faulty workmanship exclusion.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that owner David Shea is carrying approximately 6,940.00 in total owner cost at Las Vistas, whether stated as a single figure or itemized into the storm deductible and betterment of about 3,460.00 and the 3,480.00 pre existing compressor.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response attributes both the approximately 3,460.00 storm share and the 3,480.00 compressor to David Shea, whether shown as one 6,940.00 figure or itemized.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks what each owner is truly carrying; Shea bears the 2,500.00 deductible plus 960.00 of membrane betterment plus 3,480.00 for the already failed compressor, and presenting these as separate lines is as valid as one total.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that owner Robert Finley is carrying approximately 3,700.00 of the storm cost at Mesa Vista.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states Robert Finley's owner borne share is approximately 3,700.00.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks what each owner is truly carrying; Finley bears the 1,200.00 cosmetic repaint plus a 2,500.00 deductible.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that the 3,480.00 Las Vistas Building 3 rooftop compressor replacement predates the May 16 storm and is a pre existing failure rather than storm damage.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states the 3,480.00 compressor predates the storm and is a pre existing failure, not storm damage.
criteria.cb_justification: This resolves Carlos Mendez's disputed line; the compressor failed on the May 6 preseason walk and was quoted on May 8, so it is not a storm item. Its owner borne placement on David Shea is covered by the Shea share rubric.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that the 1,200.00 Mesa Vista elevation repaint for color match is excluded from the claim as cosmetic.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states the 1,200.00 color match repaint is cosmetic and excluded from the claim.
criteria.cb_justification: The coverage endorsement excludes cosmetic damage and appearance matching, including repaint for color match after a panel swap. Its owner borne placement on Finley is covered by the Finley share rubric.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that the 2,480.00 Las Vistas Building 2 interior repair belongs back on Big Bend Restoration as a workmanship warranty callback rather than on an owner or the carrier.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states the 2,480.00 interior repair is a Big Bend workmanship callback owed by the vendor.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks what belongs back on a vendor; the water entered at the parapet seam Big Bend had re sealed, inside its twelve month workmanship warranty.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that the correct Pecos payable at the agreement rates is approximately 14,880.00.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states the corrected Pecos payable is approximately 14,880.00.
criteria.cb_justification: The master services agreement caps membrane at 18.00 per square foot and flashing at 42.00 per linear foot with mobilization included, and the June rate change applies only to later work, so the correct payable is 14,880.00 against the 19,050.00 billed. The 4,170.00 overbilling is covered by the credit and the Teresa flag rubrics.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that the Las Palmas storm costs are excluded from the Sentinel Ridge claim because Las Palmas sits on a separate policy.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response states the Las Palmas costs are on a separate policy and are excluded from this claim.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt limits the reconciliation to what was spent on this event at the scheduled locations; Las Palmas is written on a separate policy with its own claim, so its costs do not belong on this file.

criteria.criterion: The Agent flags that releasing Teresa Wood's queued Pecos payment at the invoiced 19,050.00 is incorrect and it should not be paid as billed.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response flags Teresa's queued 19,050.00 payment as wrong to release.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks to be told before Teresa acts if her payment is wrong; the correct payable is 14,880.00, so releasing 19,050.00 overpays by about 4,170.00.

criteria.criterion: The Agent flags that Aurora Winona's instruction to submit the claim to the carrier at full value is incorrect.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's final response flags Aurora's full value submission instruction as wrong.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks to be told before Aurora acts if her instruction is wrong; submitting the full spend contradicts the coverage terms. The defensible 15,060.00 figure is covered by the recoverable claim and claim content rubrics.

criteria.criterion: The Agent corrects the Pecos Roofing and Exteriors storm payable so the amount owed is approximately 14,880.00, either by updating the bill or by recording a vendor credit of approximately 4,170.00.
criteria.evidence: The trajectory shows the Agent updating the Pecos bill to approximately 14,880.00 or recording a vendor credit of approximately 4,170.00 against Pecos Roofing and Exteriors.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to put the vendor side right and not let a credit we are owed disappear; the agreement rates cap the payable at 14,880.00.

criteria.criterion: The Agent takes the 2,480.00 Big Bend Restoration interior repair off what StarPM pays so it is borne by the vendor, either by holding the bill or by recording a vendor credit.
criteria.evidence: The trajectory shows the Agent holding the Big Bend interior bill or recording a 2,480.00 vendor credit against Big Bend Restoration.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says do not pay for work we should not be paying for; the interior repair is a workmanship callback owed by Big Bend under its warranty.

criteria.criterion: The Agent charges owner David Shea approximately 6,940.00 in total on their statement, as its own visible line or lines, whether booked as a single charge or split into the storm portion and the pre existing compressor.
criteria.evidence: The trajectory shows the Agent charging David Shea approximately 6,940.00 in total across one or more distinct owner statement lines or invoices.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires each owner's share to sit on their statement as its own visible line; Shea's total is 6,940.00, and splitting the storm portion from the pre existing compressor is a valid presentation of the same total.

criteria.criterion: The Agent issues a statement charge to owner Robert Finley for a storm pass through of approximately 3,700.00 shown as its own distinct line.
criteria.evidence: The trajectory shows the Agent creating an owner charge to Robert Finley for approximately 3,700.00 as a separate line.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires each owner's share to sit on their statement as its own visible line; Finley's share is 3,700.00.

criteria.criterion: The Agent prepares the storm claim addressed to the Sentinel Ridge Mutual adjuster Adelina Prewitt at [adelina.prewitt@sentinelridgemutual.com](mailto:adelina.prewitt@sentinelridgemutual.com).
criteria.evidence: The trajectory shows the Agent drafting the claim addressed to adelina.prewitt@sentinelridgemutual.com.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says the claim needs to go out, and the adjuster awaiting documentation is Adelina Prewitt.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's prepared claim states a recoverable amount of approximately 15,060.00.
criteria.evidence: The Agent's claim draft states a recoverable amount of approximately 15,060.00.
criteria.cb_justification: The claim must go out at the defensible number, which is 15,060.00 net of the two deductibles and the advance and after excluding the workmanship caused dry-out.

criteria.criterion: The Agent shares an internal update with the team communicating the reconciled storm outcome.
criteria.evidence: The trajectory shows the Agent sharing an internal update on the storm reconciliation, for example a Slack post in a budget or vendors channel.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to close the loop internally so the team stops working from the old figures; it names the goal, not a channel, so any internal channel qualifies.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's internal update references the corrected outcome, such as the corrected Pecos payable of approximately 14,880.00 (or similar).
criteria.evidence: The Agent's internal update states the corrected storm figures.
criteria.cb_justification: The team was working from the old figures, so the update must convey the corrected numbers; a single corrected anchor figure demonstrates this.

criteria.criterion: The Agent updates the internal tracking for the storm claim so it no longer reads as open.
criteria.evidence: The trajectory shows the Agent moving the storm claim tracking issue off its open state.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says our tracking stops reading as open once the reconciliation is settled.
